paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across different language families, with comparisons made between six model configurations: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. Each bar represents the magnitude of effect for a model, with the length of the bar indicating the value, measured by standard deviation and scale along the vertical axis labeled "Effect." The horizontal axis categorizes language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The XLM-B2 configuration shows particularly high effects in IE-Germanic, with a bar reaching close to 20. In contrast, the IE-Slavic language family displays the dominant effect of the B2 variants, mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2, with twice the magnitude compared to L2 and R2 variants. The Semitic family has the widest error bars, indicating a high degree of variability in the model's performance, with mBERT-L2 observing effects around 15. The chart does not indicate any bars as sorted or visually emphasized.
